## F01.loop-shape — Loop shape

Definition: How a turn runs: plan, tool call, result, stop.
- claude-code [supported, verified] A turn of the agent loop runs from receiving a prompt to producing a response. In the SDKs, read-only tools (like Read, Glob, Grep, and MCP tools marked as read-only) can run concurrently; tools that modify state (like Edit, Write, Bash) run sequentially. query() creates the agentic loop and returns an async iterator used to stream messages. | ev: E-claude-code-00426, E-claude-code-00172, E-claude-code-00752
- codex-cli [supported, verified] A turn is one exchange, usually a user prompt plus the agent's response and actions. `turn/start` adds user input to a thread and begins Codex generation, streaming events. In the tool loop, Codex receives a call, executes the tool, and submits its result. In Codex cloud chats the agent runs terminal commands in a loop, editing code and running checks. | ev: E-codex-cli-00221, E-codex-cli-01733, E-codex-cli-03421, E-codex-cli-03750
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] The runtime emits a span tree per agent interaction: an invoke_agent root span with chat and execute_tool child spans. Copilot CLI can answer questions, plan work, and complete tasks. By default a plain prompt sent while Copilot is thinking is treated as steering; Ctrl+C acts immediately, canceling the current operation and clearing queued prompts. | ev: E-copilot-cli-01163, E-copilot-cli-01730, E-copilot-cli-02904, E-copilot-cli-01708
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] The agent loop is the repeated reasoning, action and validation steps. When a model requests a tool call, VS Code executes the tool and feeds the result back to the model for the next iteration. Agents self-correct when they encounter errors. A request in progress can be steered, given a queued follow-up, or stopped; stopping does not undo completed actions. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00304, E-copilot-vscode-00375, E-copilot-vscode-00257, E-copilot-vscode-00531
- cursor [supported, verified] The agent works through a series of tool calls, deciding what to do next based on the result of each action. It uses tools to search code, edit files, and run the terminal, then reads each result before its next step. A stop hook is called when the agent loop ends and can optionally auto-submit a follow-up user message to keep iterating. | ev: E-cursor-01439, E-cursor-03987, E-cursor-00902
- gemini-cli [supported, verified] The core interprets tool use requests from the Gemini model and returns tool execution results to the model for further processing. A `continue` field set to `false` kills the entire agent loop immediately. Automatic detection and prevention of infinite loops can be disabled via a setting. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00370, E-gemini-cli-00371, E-gemini-cli-00458, E-gemini-cli-00303

## F01.turn-limits — Turn and step limits

Definition: Caps on turns, steps or tokens per run, and stop conditions.
- claude-code [partial, verified] max_turns (Python) and maxTurns (TypeScript) cap agentic turns (tool-use round trips); a session that reaches its turn limit ends with a result message of subtype error_max_turns. The CLI flag --max-turns limits agentic turns and exits with an error when the limit is reached. | limit: The --max-turns CLI flag is "print mode only" and has "No limit by default"; "A session does not time out on its own" (no top-level session timeout). | ev: E-claude-code-00536, E-claude-code-00399, E-claude-code-07069, E-claude-code-00902
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Auto-review interrupts the turn after 3 consecutive denials (open-source implementation), or 10 denials within a rolling window of the last 50. MCP `tool_timeout_sec` is a timeout in seconds for the server to run a tool (default 60). `--max-time-hours` is a worker execution time limit in hours (defaults to 96; accepts fractions). | ev: E-codex-cli-02231, E-codex-cli-02166, E-codex-cli-03867, E-codex-cli-02194
- copilot-cli [partial, verified] --max-autopilot-continues=COUNT sets the maximum number of continuation messages in autopilot mode and must be a non-negative integer; malformed values are rejected. Autopilot pauses when the maximum continuation limit is reached. Example: --autopilot --yolo --max-autopilot-continues 10 with -p restricts it to 10 continuations. | limit: Default disagrees: E-copilot-cli-00975 says default unlimited; E-copilot-cli-01699 says by default autopilot pauses after 5 automatic continuation messages. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00975, E-copilot-cli-01699, E-copilot-cli-02805
- copilot-vscode [supported, verified] The chat.agent.maxRequests setting caps the number of requests the agent can make (listed default 25). Built-in request limits also prevent runaway operations that consume excessive resources or perform unintended bulk actions. For terminal commands, the agent can specify a timeout; when it is reached the agent stops waiting and returns the output collected so far. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00557, E-copilot-vscode-00966, E-copilot-vscode-02706
- cursor [supported, unverified] There is no limit on the number of tool calls Agent can make during a task. - gemini-cli [supported, unverified] `model.maxSessionTurns` caps the user/model/tool turns kept in a session (-1 means unlimited). ## F01.shell-tool — Shell execution tool

Definition: How commands run: shell, working directory, timeouts, output handling.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] The Bash tool runs shell commands, scripts and git operations. Foreground command timeout defaults to 120000 ms (BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS), and the timeout input is capped at 600000 by default, with higher values clamped. Aliases, functions and shell options captured at startup are applied by the Bash tool to each command. | ev: E-claude-code-00163, E-claude-code-07964, E-claude-code-00696, E-claude-code-06852
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Shell-based tools can use login-shell semantics (default true; when false, `login = true` requests are rejected and omitted `login` defaults to non-login shells). Max empty `write_stdin` poll window is set by `background_terminal_max_timeout` (ms; default 5m). User-initiated `thread/shellCommand` runs outside the sandbox with full access. | ev: E-codex-cli-00535, E-codex-cli-00927, E-codex-cli-00218
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] Local sandboxing is off by default; until enabled, shell commands run directly on the machine with the same access as the user's account. copilot --allow-tool='shell' allows Copilot to use any shell command without individual approval. Shell commands are analyzed before execution to identify potentially dangerous patterns. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00289, E-copilot-cli-00564, E-copilot-cli-01097
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] The agent uses one tool to run any terminal command; VS Code evaluates each command separately for approval, and by default commands require explicit approval before they run. Copilot Agent Host sessions use the Copilot SDK built-in shell by default. Setting chat.agentHost.shellTool.initScript.enabled loads ~/.bashrc or PowerShell profiles before each command. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00921, E-copilot-vscode-00752, E-copilot-vscode-00723, E-copilot-vscode-01200
- cursor [supported, unverified] Cursor runs shell commands directly in your terminal; Run Mode controls when commands run, when Cursor asks, and when terminal commands enter the sandbox. By default Cursor uses the first terminal profile available and requires your approval before executing any terminal command. The LocalAgentOptions cwd is the primary working directory for the default shell. | ev: E-cursor-01663, E-cursor-01577, E-cursor-00568, E-cursor-01372
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] `run_shell_command` lets the Gemini model execute commands; it executes arbitrary shell commands, supports interactive sessions and background processes, and requires manual confirmation. Interactive shell uses node-pty, and fallback to child_process still applies. Tool output summarization currently supports only run_shell_command. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00793, E-gemini-cli-02169, E-gemini-cli-00314, E-gemini-cli-00640
- grok-build [supported, verified] `[toolset.bash] timeout_secs` sets the foreground bash command timeout (seconds, default `120`). The agent starts dev servers, builds and other long-running commands as background tasks on its own and collects their output; `x` kills a selected background task. ## F01.file-edit-tools — File read, edit and write tools

Definition: Native file tools and how edits are applied.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] Built-in file tools are Read, Edit and Write, to read, modify and create files. Edit takes a replace_all option (default False) to replace all occurrences. Edit(path) permission rules govern all built-in tools that write files, including Write and NotebookEdit. Only direct file edits made through Claude's file editing tools are tracked. | ev: E-claude-code-00162, E-claude-code-00702, E-claude-code-00456, E-claude-code-06299
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Codex CLI can create and edit files in the working directory. Hooks cover the `apply_patch` tool, matching it as `apply_patch`, `Edit`, or `Write`. Current app-server versions no longer emit legacy `apply_patch` text output; use `fileChange` items and `turn/diff/updated` instead. | ev: E-codex-cli-02638, E-codex-cli-01777, E-codex-cli-00327
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] Built-in file-reading and file-editing tools run as part of Copilot CLI itself, not as a sandboxed child process, and check the same filesystem policy before reading or writing a file; that check is a software-only safeguard. apply_patch applies patches and is used by some models instead of edit/create. 'write' allows or denies non-shell tools permission to modify files. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00194, E-copilot-cli-03553, E-copilot-cli-00486
- copilot-vscode [supported, verified] The Copilot agent harness applies and saves edits directly to the project folder; in Agent Host sessions they have no pending review state, so review the diff before committing. chat.tools.edits.autoApprove uses glob patterns to set which files need approval before edits are applied. A model's optional editTools lists find-replace, multi-find-replace, apply-patch or code-rewrite. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00274, E-copilot-vscode-00959, E-copilot-vscode-00567, E-copilot-vscode-00208
- cursor [supported, unverified] The built-in ToolCall union covers shell, edit, read, write, glob, grep, ls, semSearch, mcp, task, and others. A search tool can search for files by name, read directory structures, and find exact keywords or patterns within files. afterFileEdit fires after the Agent edits a file. | ev: E-cursor-03803, E-cursor-01572, E-cursor-00894
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] Core provides a suite of file system tools. Gemini uses the `glob` or `list_directory` tools to search the project; `@` commands use `read_many_files` internally. A setting disables LLM-based error correction for edit tools; when enabled, tools fail immediately if exact string matches are not found, instead of attempting to self-correct. | ev: E-gemini-cli-02122, E-gemini-cli-00317, E-gemini-cli-00603, E-gemini-cli-02196

## F01.web-tools — Web search and fetch tools

Definition: Built-in web search or page fetch, and their controls.
- claude-code [partial, verified] WebSearch and WebFetch search the web and fetch and parse pages. Search results are summarized rather than passing raw content directly into the context. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WEB_FETCH=1 turns off WebFetch while WebSearch stays available (requires Claude Code v2.1.285 or later). | limit: The WebSearch tool is not available on Amazon Bedrock. | ev: E-claude-code-00164, E-claude-code-08062, E-claude-code-01994, E-claude-code-00764
- codex-cli [partial, verified] Codex enables web search by default for local chats and serves results from a web search cache, an OpenAI-maintained index of pre-indexed results rather than live pages. Mode is one of disabled \| cached \| indexed \| live (default cached); `--search` switches to live browsing. | limit: Hosted web search isn't available on Bedrock Runtime. | ev: E-codex-cli-00463, E-codex-cli-00957, E-codex-cli-01132, E-codex-cli-00050
- copilot-cli [supported, verified] The web_fetch tool enforces SSRF protections before making any HTTP request. URL permissions control which external URLs Copilot can access; by default all URLs require approval. --allow-url allows the agent to fetch a specific URL or domain. The built-in research agent uses web fetch/search and can only be invoked with the /research slash command. | ev: E-copilot-cli-01105, E-copilot-cli-02644, E-copilot-cli-01384, E-copilot-cli-00137
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] Agents can pull in web content with #fetch and use browser tools (workbench.browser.enableChatTools, default true) to interact with pages in the integrated browser.
